questions.text: Which statement accurately describes the architectural distinction between Electron's main process and renderer process?
options: The renderer process creates native OS windows and manages application lifecycles, while the main process executes the webpage DOM.
The main process runs in Node.js to manage native OS integration and windows, while renderer processes run Chromium to render web interfaces.
Both processes share the same JavaScript global scope and can access Node.js built-ins without IPC.
Electron spins up a separate main process for each BrowserWindow opened by the application.

questions.text: What is the primary security benefit of using `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld()` in a preload script?
options: It accelerates DOM tree rendering by bypassing Chromium security boundaries.
It safely exposes a selective API to the renderer without leaking full Node.js or Electron internals across the execution context.
It automatically encrypts all HTTP network requests initiated by the renderer.
It binds the client window directly to the operating system's kernel.

questions.text: How do `ipcMain.handle()` and `ipcRenderer.invoke()` coordinate two-way asynchronous communication?
options: ipcRenderer.invoke() sends a blocking call that freezes the renderer until ipcMain.handle() responds.
ipcMain.handle() registers a request-response handler whose return value resolves the Promise returned by ipcRenderer.invoke().
ipcMain.handle() can only transmit string payloads and cannot serialize JavaScript objects.
ipcRenderer.invoke() requires a separate ipcRenderer.on() listener to capture the return value.

questions.text: What protection does `contextIsolation: true` provide in BrowserWindow webPreferences?
options: It ensures preload scripts and website scripts run in separate JavaScript contexts, preventing webpage code from mutating preload prototypes or hijacking exposed objects.
It blocks the preload script from requiring any CommonJS modules.
It isolates the webpage completely from Chromium's CSS engine.
It prevents the main process from sending push messages to the renderer.

questions.text: Which Electron module and method should be used to display an OS-native modal file selection or alert dialog attached to a specific BrowserWindow?
options: window.alert() and window.confirm() in the renderer process
dialog.showMessageBox(win, options) or dialog.showOpenDialog(win, options) in the main process
shell.openPath(win, options) in the main process
app.showModal(win, options) in the main process

questions.text: Why is an 'Edit' menu containing standard roles (`undo`, `copy`, `paste`) required in macOS Electron applications?
options: macOS requires an Edit menu to allocate GPU memory buffers for text rendering.
Without an Edit menu with standard roles, keyboard shortcuts like Cmd+C, Cmd+V, and Cmd+X do not work inside text inputs on macOS.
The macOS App Store automatically rejects apps that attach custom keyboard event listeners.
Without an Edit menu, right-click context menus cannot be rendered.

questions.text: How can an Electron main process detect and react to operating system dark mode and light mode changes?
options: By polling window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') from the Node.js runtime
By reading process.env.MACOS_THEME on an interval
By listening to nativeTheme.on('updated') and checking nativeTheme.shouldUseDarkColors
Electron cannot inspect OS theme preferences without native C++ addons

questions.text: When exporting sensitive data (such as exam audit logs or certificates) to disk in Electron, which approach is the security best practice?
options: Enable nodeIntegration in the renderer and use the Node.js 'fs' module directly from UI button click handlers.
Send an export command over IPC to main, prompt the user with dialog.showSaveDialog, and write using fs.promises in the main process.
Generate a client-side data: URI anchor tag to trigger a silent download in the renderer.
Write the file directly into process.cwd() without path or permission checks.

questions.text: Where should an Electron application write persistent user configurations, logs, and local databases across app updates?
options: Inside the application package directory (__dirname)
Directly in the operating system /tmp directory
In the designated path returned by app.getPath('userData')
In the system root directory /

questions.text: Which statement is true regarding Electron's main-process `Notification` API?
options: It renders floating HTML divs inside the active BrowserWindow DOM.
It displays native desktop notifications through the host operating system's notification center.
It requires Chromium's Web Notification permission prompt in the renderer.
It can only be invoked when the application window is running in fullscreen mode.

questions.text: When launching system CLI tools or background commands using Node's `child_process` in Electron, what is a critical security precaution?
options: Always use child_process.exec() with string concatenation of untrusted inputs.
Prefer child_process.execFile() or spawn() with explicit argument arrays without a shell interpreter to prevent command injection.
child_process can only be invoked from web workers in the renderer.
Always execute spawned child processes with elevated root/sudo privileges.

questions.text: How can an Electron application intercept and restrict Chromium media and hardware device permission requests (e.g. webcam, microphone)?
options: By disabling JavaScript in BrowserWindow webPreferences
By configuring session.defaultSession.setPermissionRequestHandler() and setPermissionCheckHandler() to inspect origin and permission types
By hiding navigator.mediaDevices using CSS rules in the renderer
Chromium permissions cannot be controlled by the Electron main process

questions.text: What primary defense does a strict Content Security Policy (`script-src 'self'`) enforce in an Electron renderer process?
options: It prevents Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) by blocking execution of untrusted inline scripts and external remote scripts.
It automatically minifies and compresses React component bundles.
It disables all modern CSS properties including Flexbox and Grid.
It encrypts IPC message payloads between the renderer and main process.

questions.text: What is the correct sequential order of Electron lifecycle events when an application is terminated?
options: quit -> will-quit -> close -> before-quit
before-quit -> close (for each window) -> will-quit -> quit
close -> before-quit -> quit -> will-quit
will-quit -> before-quit -> close -> quit

questions.text: When packaging an Electron desktop application for production with electron-builder, what purpose does an ASAR archive serve?
options: An encrypted machine binary executed by the host CPU.
A read-only archive format that packages application source code into a single file to prevent long path issues on Windows and speed up reads.
A proprietary macOS code-signing certificate container.
An embedded Docker container runtime bundled inside the executable.
